analysis.title: US Equities Weekly Rundown: Positioning, Flows, and Observations Across the Floor
key_insights: S&P 500 rose 1.2% on the week to 7,811.54 ahead of 3Q earnings season and next Tuesday's CPI report. IPPs, AI Software and Power Infrastructure outperformed. NeoClouds, Bitcoin Sensitive equities and Non-Profitable Tech underperformed.

Prime book: US equities were slightly net sold (-0.1 SDs 1-year), with short sales outpacing long buys in single stocks. Single stocks were net sold for a third straight week (-0.3 SDs), with short sales to long buys at 2 to 1.

Hedge funds rotated into Industrials and out of Info Tech, most notably on Thursday Oct 8. After five straight weeks of selling, HFs bought Industrials at the fastest pace since early January (+1.8 SDs), almost entirely long buys. Info Tech was the most net sold sector (-1.0 SDs) on long and short sales, which the desk reads as profit taking and hedging.

Health Care saw de-grossing for a 4th straight week, with short covers outpacing long sales 1.6 to 1. Biotech has seen risk unwinds in 7 of the past 8 weeks, and its 8-week de-grossing is the largest in more than five years. Biotech long/short ratio is 3.22 versus a peak of 5.36 in Dec 2025.

US L/S gross leverage rose 3.8 pts to 213% (53rd percentile one-year). Net leverage rose 0.5 pts to 46.9% (2nd percentile one-year), its first increase in four weeks. The fundamental long/short ratio fell to 1.565 (1st percentile five-year).

Shares desk: a heavy wave of selling hit Semis and AI on Thursday around OpenAI revenue headlines and continued Friday despite a clarification. The desk calls the Friday snapback another example of high-velocity AI sentiment swings. It also saw long supply in Telcos on the SPCX announcement and profit-taking in Managed Care after the Medicare STARs results.

3Q earnings: consensus growth is +27% y/y, the highest estimate since 2021, while the median stock is expected at +9% y/y versus 14% in Q2. Beats were rewarded with only 35bps of outperformance versus the S&P last quarter, against 95bps historically.

Mag7 positioning on the GS Prime book moved from a YTD low of 14% of US exposure in June to a record 22%. The desk notes MU beat across the board with a muted reaction and asks whether this signals a high-bar dynamic across AI.

Futures: Nasdaq's funding premium to the S&P reached a 98% one-year rank on Oct 8, suggesting leveraged long positioning increased even as the rally stalled. Asset managers sold $3.2bn of index futures from Sep 8 to 29 alongside higher prices, which took the correlation between asset manager gross longs and price to roughly nil.

Gold rose 1.3% WoW and held above $4,100/oz. Systematic strategies are at the 0th percentile of positioning on a one-year lookback, and CFTC managed-money net length is back to average. The futures desk says adding gold length looks increasingly attractive.

Long bonds may have bottomed after selling off since Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole speech on 8/28. Bond futures rallied Thursday on the OpenAI revenue restatement headlines. The desk links higher long-term yields to expected AI-related bond issuance competing with government supply. Asset manager shorts in the long bond rose sharply since mid-September, and covering could support bonds into early next week.

Financials earnings: XLF is -6.5% from highs despite SPX records. The ratio of recent drawdown to earnings straddle is about 5x, so implied earnings moves look cheap. Implied moves: MS 3.7%, BAC 3.4%, WFC 4.8%, C 3.5%.

Index skew: VIX upside convexity is extremely bid while SPX downside convexity stays offered. An index vol desk colleague said there is almost a higher probability of VIX 25+ than of SPX -2%. This reflects very low realized correlation and very high dispersion.

Most index implied vols finished the week near 2-3 month lows. QQQ vol fell while QQQ spot rose, so there was no upside squeeze. Call demand was concentrated in small caps. RTY futures positioning is at record shorts, IWM short interest is at a record high, and IWM vol is below the 10th percentile. The desk likes owning calls to protect short small-cap delta.

EWZ traded over $8bn on Monday, the largest notional day in the fund's 25-year history, and had a record +$700m daily inflow. AUM is above $11bn with more than $2bn gathered since the start of the week. The underlying index is on track for its best week since 2020, and EWZS (Brazilian small caps) also drew interest. Brazil's presidential runoff is Oct 25.

SPW/SPX (equal weight versus cap weight) is at multi-decade lows, but RSP demand was strong Thursday and the SPW vs SPX pair had its best session since summer (+1%). SPY and RSP overlap is near 20-year lows.

Fixed income ETFs account for over 20% of ETF volume over the past 10 sessions, nearly double the share from months prior, as rates hit multi-year highs. Muni funds took more than $4.5bn of inflows in October after a record September.

Baskets desk likes buying the Power Up America basket (GSENEPOW), calling power the most underappreciated AI bottleneck with low positioning, normalized valuation and intact fundamentals. Positioning and IPP valuations are at 2-year lows. Dated catalysts: FERC ruling on the PJM large-load framework (Oct 12), PJM RBP filings, and the ERCOT data center interconnection audit.

TMT: NDX is up 4 weeks in a row and 6 of 7, but Software outperformed Semis by about 800 bps this week. Franchise activity pointed to profit taking or hedging, as optimism on earnings is balanced by questions on execution, expectations and linearity. TSM and ASML report next week, alongside WDAY and ACN analyst days and Semicon West (AMAT, LRCX).

Financials sector: outperformed, led by Exchanges, diversified P&C insurers and Payments/Fintech. Big banks report Tuesday with sentiment notably cautious. Investors are tactically positive on net interest margins, helped by lagging deposit repricing through end-2026, though 2027 is debated. Credit risk is viewed as benign, with one eye on CRE.

Healthcare: Medicare Advantage 2027 STARs results were mostly in line with previews. HUM rose 13% and ALHC fell 12% after losing 4 stars in its largest plan. Tools fell (GSHLCTOO -4%) as AI drug discovery took a breather. Biopharma movers: PCVX +31%, TEVA +6%, PCRX +44%, AVBP -47%, RVMD -6%.

Industrials and Materials: Industrials -30bps and Materials +150bps on the week. Industrials are at multi-year lows relative to the market while PMIs remain in growth mode. RXO rose 24% on a takeout bid from CHRW. CTVA rose 11% after spinning out VYLR. CNH fell 15% after WASDE pushed corn prices lower. QXO fell 11% on rate-driven housing weakness. DAL kicked off earnings with a miss and cut but fell only 100bps. FAST and JBHT report next week.

Last quarter beats were frequent but rewarded with only 35bps of outperformance versus the S&P, against 95bps historically.
MU reported a beat across the board (already printed) with a muted stock reaction. The desk asks whether this reflects a high-bar dynamic across AI.

About 7% of SPX constituents report by next Friday, including 43% of financials market cap, 16% of healthcare market cap and 11% of real estate market cap. Tech starts later in October.
TSM and ASML report next week. FAST and JBHT also report next week.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Markets await the next Fed move, and the CPI print is the main data event next week.
Yield is at multi-year highs, and fixed income ETF volumes have surged as total returns turned negative in several segments.
Very low realized correlation alongside very high dispersion is reflected in cheap SPX downside convexity and bid VIX upside.

crypto_views: Bitcoin was 82,334.07 on the week, -2.5% WoW and -6.1% YTD.
The Bitcoin Sensitive equities basket (GSCBBTC1) fell 7.70% on the week, among the worst performers, though it is +35.21% YTD.
